newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - EMU helps German firms little on rates.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - EMU helps German firms little on rates.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Monday that German companies would have the least to win in terms of interest rates with the launch of the new single European currency, slated to start in January 1999.

"It is true that German companies would lose a special advantage," Tietmeyer, referring to a new Euro leading to an expanded European capital market, said in the text of a speech to a reception at the IAA truck exhibition in Hanover.
He said that the earlier privilege of having their home currency viewed as a reserve currency would be lost against competitors from currency member countries.
